## Overview:
The PR changes `Cache.get` to return a value plus staleness metadata via `readWithMetadata`, while retaining `null` for misses. The profile loader’s cache-hit logic is otherwise unchanged.

The main risk area is downstream compatibility: callers that previously received a string now receive an object. In particular, `loadProfile` still passes the cached result directly to `JSON.parse`, warranting specialist review of cache-hit behavior and affected contracts.

## Strengths:
- Small, focused implementation change.
- Preserves the existing cache-miss representation (`null`).
- Introduces metadata without changing the underlying async API shape.

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR changes `Cache.get` in `src/cache.ts` to return staleness metadata: instead of `Promise<string | null>` backed by `store.read(key)`, it now returns `Promise<{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null>` backed by `store.readWithMetadata(key)`. The cache-miss representation (`null`) is preserved, and `loadProfile` in `src/profile.ts` is re-touched but its logic is textually unchanged.

The intent — surfacing staleness while preserving contracts — is reasonable, but the return-type change breaks the only caller: `loadProfile` still passes the cache result directly to `JSON.parse`, which now receives an `{ value, stale }` object on every cache hit. That contract break is blocking; the rest of the change is sound.

findings.title: [P1] Parse `cached.value` instead of the `{ value, stale }` wrapper
findings.body: Requires any cache hit. `Cache.get` now returns `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null` (`src/cache.ts:5-6`), so on a hit `cached` is a truthy object and `src/profile.ts:19` executes `JSON.parse(cached)` with a non-string. This is a TypeScript type error, and in emitted JavaScript `JSON.parse` coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws `SyntaxError`, so `loadProfile` rejects instead of returning the cached profile. Fix: `if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached.value);`.

findings.body: The new `stale` metadata returned by `readWithMetadata` (`src/cache.ts:5-6`) is read by nothing — `loadProfile` is the only caller of `cache.get` and ignores it, so stale entries are served exactly like fresh ones. If refresh-on-stale handling is planned for a follow-up, fine; otherwise the flag is dead surface on this contract.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR changes `Cache.get` in `src/cache.ts` to return staleness metadata: instead of `Promise<string | null>` backed by `store.read(key)`, it now returns `Promise<{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null>` backed by `store.readWithMetadata(key)`. The cache-miss representation (`null`) is preserved, and `loadProfile` in `src/profile.ts` is re-touched but its logic is textually unchanged.

The intent — surfacing staleness while preserving contracts — is reasonable, but the return-type change breaks the only caller: `loadProfile` still passes the cache result directly to `JSON.parse`, which now receives an `{ value, stale }` object on every cache hit. That contract break is blocking; the rest of the change is sound.

## Verification

Skipped — no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured, so `pr_review_verify` (`action: list`) reported verification disabled and no baseline was run. Note: baseline execution runs PR code unsandboxed (supervision covers only the original POSIX process group); an external sandbox/container wrapper is recommended for untrusted PRs if verification is enabled later. Findings above were validated directly against the diff and the head checkout instead.

## Findings

### [P1] Parse `cached.value` instead of the `{ value, stale }` wrapper
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** Requires any cache hit. `Cache.get` now returns `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null` (`src/cache.ts:5-6`), so on a hit `cached` is a truthy object and `src/profile.ts:19` executes `JSON.parse(cached)` with a non-string. This is a TypeScript type error, and in emitted JavaScript `JSON.parse` coerces the object to `"[object Object]"` and throws `SyntaxError`, so `loadProfile` rejects instead of returning the cached profile. Fix: `if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached.value);`.
**Location:** `src/profile.ts:19-19 RIGHT`

### [P3] Confirm intended: new `stale` flag has no consumer
**Severity:** P3
**Rationale:** The new `stale` metadata returned by `readWithMetadata` (`src/cache.ts:5-6`) is read by nothing — `loadProfile` is the only caller of `cache.get` and ignores it, so stale entries are served exactly like fresh ones. If refresh-on-stale handling is planned for a follow-up, fine; otherwise the flag is dead surface on this contract.
**Location:** `src/cache.ts:5-6 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

The `conventions-maintainability` pass failed on first dispatch (transient upstream server overload); it was rerun individually with the same tier and tool policy and completed successfully, so its evidence is included. All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes

- Small, focused diff; the miss contract (`null`) and the async API shape are preserved.
- The new return type honestly declares the richer `readWithMetadata` result rather than hiding it.
- **Correctness:** one blocking defect — the P1 cache-hit break above; `overall_correctness` is "patch is incorrect" until `cached.value` is parsed. No provable stale-refresh regression was found (no `store` implementation exists to compare old vs. new stale semantics).
- **Security:** no security regressions in the changed code.
- **Performance:** no resource, allocation, or I/O regressions introduced.
